subject: GPU commitment worksheet and session profile — Ardent AI
body:
From: Alex Smith <alex.smith@ardentai.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@ardentai.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU plan for Ardent — initial metrics

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for the demo last week. We’re excited to move toward a committed plan for Q1. To give your sizing folks something concrete, here are a few baseline numbers from our production traces: 

- Avg steady-state requests: 18 req/s
- Peak sustained window: 110 req/s for ~12 minutes, 3x/day
- P99 latency target: 300 ms (inference-only)
- Typical prompt tokens: 80
- Typical response tokens: 320
- Session stickiness: ~55% sessions are multi-turn (avg turns per session = 4)

Two questions for you: 1) Is reserving 8 x A100-equivalent GPUs reasonable for our commit level? 2) Do you want the full token distribution or a sample CSV? 

— Alex
Senior ML Engineer, Ardent AI

-----Original Message-----
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Alex Smith <alex.smith@ardentai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated GPU plan for Ardent — initial ask

Alex —

Great meeting — follow-up to get us the concrete telemetry so we can finish the Dedicated sizing worksheet. If you can paste a week of request traces (timestamp, prompt_len, response_len, model_id, avg_user_wait_ms) that helps a lot. If not, a 95/99 token percentiles + burst cadence will do.

We typically convert that inside our sizing model into: steady qps, peak burst profile (duration + magnitude), session affinity ratio, and token-per-inference distribution. From that we map to GPU sku + oversubscription plan and recommend an autoscale guardrail.

I attached our commitment worksheet (blank) — fill the green fields and send back. Also confirm whether you need GPU isolation (dedicated pool) vs. reserved but shared within your tenant.

Regards,
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Hi all,

Attached a 48-hour sample (session_profile_sample.csv) and the signed commitment worksheet draft (ardentai_gpu_commitment_worksheet.xlsx). The CSV includes session ids so you can calculate stickiness. Quick notes:

- The 110 req/s peak came from a regional campaign (east US) and lasted ~12 minutes.
- We have soft real-time prep that pads response tokens by ~15–20 tokens on the server side.
- We prefer NVIDIA H100-class equivalence due to perf with long context.

Let us know the sizing output and any flags before we submit to Procurement.

— Alex

-- Marissa runs sizing model and posts results
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Smith <alex.smith@ardentai.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:38:00 -0800
Subject: Re: GPU commitment worksheet and session profile — Ardent AI

Alex —

Thanks for the CSV and the worksheet. Quick summary of the model run (provisional):

- Effective steady QPS (workload-normalized): 20 req/s
- Burst model: 3x steady for 12 min, daily x3 -> recommendation includes a short-term burst buffer
- Multi-turn impact: ~55% multi-turn => KV cache reuse expected, reduces per-token compute by ~18% compared to stateless baseline
- Token distribution (median): prompt 78 / response 326. 95th: prompt 220 / response 740

Sizing recommendation (provisional):
- Recommended committed footprint: 6 x H100-equivalent GPUs with 20% burst headroom mapped to a burst pool (managed autoscale)
- If you require absolute isolation per-tenant, add 1 GPU for redundancy (7 total)
- Suggested oversubscription: 1.2x for steady background, fallback routing to smaller model variants under overloaded conditions

I attached the annotated worksheet with the numbers filled. Can you confirm whether you need on-prem/KMS integration and whether your procurement prefers monthly or annual commit? These affect discount tiers.

Marissa

We’re ready to move but need clarity on discount bands and SLA credits for P99 > 400 ms. Also confirm whether burst autoscale will be billed as usage over commit or if there’s a capped burst allowance.

Team —

Quick recap for contract threading: 
- Provisional sizing: 6 H100-eq GPUs (7 if strict isolation)
- Billing model preference needed: monthly vs annual commit (affects discount)
- Burst handling: recommend capped burst pool billed as overage; propose a 10% capped free burst per month as a negotiation lever
- SLA ask: Procurement expects P99 <= 400 ms or credits. Our current suggested target meets 300 ms for inference-only in steady state. Need legal on credit language.

Can Ben/Karthik propose discount tiers and a brief redline for the burst allowance? I’ll reply to Procurement and loop legal once you draft.

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
